For a rule with 100+ importing/call-site files, the productive strategy is: read the rule's OWN helper functions for internal asymmetries first, THEN grep the corpus only for the specific shapes that asymmetry predicts.
A rule's own .test.ts file is authoritative for whether a behavior is a known/intended limitation vs an undiscovered bug - always check the test file before filing an issue about a suspected gap.

Issues auto-expire (~1wk TTL) and get bot-closed as not_planned - a single expiry is NOT reliably 'unfixed housekeeping': multiple confirmed instances of a fix landing in the same window as expiry. ALWAYS re-read the current rule source before deciding to refile an expired item.

Bash sandbox flags multi-command chains, xargs, sort, printf-with-newlines, some grep -E patterns, and for-loops with variable expansion as 'contains expansion'/'multiple operations requiring approval' even with zero actual shell variables - prefer the Grep/Glob/Read tools over Bash for exploratory searching; reserve Bash for single simple gh/git one-liners. Grep tool also rejects lookaround (?<!...) - PCRE2 not supported, use plain character-class negation instead. Grep tool's glob param does NOT support extglob negation like `!(*.test).cjs` - it silently matches everything; filter test files out of results manually instead.
